item.text:
**1B.2 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

I found no credible 2024 evidence that Srettha Thavisin used reckless nuclear threats, brinkmanship, apocalyptic language, or normalized nuclear use. The record is mostly peace-oriented and disarmament-oriented; the only explicit nuclear mention I found was in a civilian/clean-energy context.

|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Thailand co-chaired the 15th ASEAN Regional Forum Inter-Sessional Meeting on Non-Proliferation and Disarmament in Honolulu, Hawaii](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | May 3, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand’s official line under Srettha’s government supported strengthening and transparency in nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament, explicitly aiming at the total elimination of nuclear weapons. This is strong positive evidence for restrained, responsible nuclear rhetoric. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| [Statement of Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand at the Summit for Democracy, 20 March 2024](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-statement-2024?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 20, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-statement-2024?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848 | Srettha’s public rhetoric in this official statement emphasized democracy, rule of law, human rights, and responsible foreign relations. I found no nuclear-threat, brinkmanship, or apocalyptic framing in the statement. | `1B.2` |

That is consistent with responsible rhetoric and not with nuclear saber-rattling. | `1B.2` |
| [Readout of Secretary Raimondo’s Meeting with Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha) | U.S. Department of Commerce | March 14, 2024 | https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha | The only explicit nuclear reference I found in 2024 Srettha-related material was cooperation on civil nuclear energy, discussed alongside clean energy and sustainability. That is peaceful civilian framing, not militarized rhetoric. | `1B.2` |

**Search gap**
- I did not find any reliable 2024 source showing Srettha using nuclear threats, nuclear brinkmanship, or apocalyptic nuclear language.
- I also did not find any 2024 source where he normalized nuclear use or hinted at escalation for prestige or leverage.
- The evidence base is therefore asymmetric: several responsible/peace-oriented or civilian nuclear references, but no credible contrary examples in the sources searched.
